summary: Generics let one class or method work with any type while the compiler still checks types. Box<String> can only hold a String, and get() returns a String with no cast.
notes: static <T> T firstItem(List<T> items) declares T before the return type. Java infers T from the argument.
new Box<>("Calculator") uses the diamond <>. The compiler copies the type from the left side.
Type parameters must be object types: Box<Integer> works, Box<int> does not compile.
pitfall: Writing new Box<String>(404) fails at compile time with incompatible types: int cannot be converted to String. That is the point: the error appears before the program runs.
